title: projects.json
description: The source of truth for which projects exist and what each one opens: a project is a set of kitty windows in one Hyprland group on the `code` scene, and `path`/`windows`/`workspace` here are the template `,proj.sh open` reads at runtime. The list is hand-curated and nothing discovers projects: `,proj.sh add <name> [path]` is the deliberate inclusion of a directory (it also folds the repo's own `.proj.toml` in), `drop` removes one, and `,proj.sh sync` only refreshes what each stored project's own `.proj.toml` declares (`windows`/`workspace`/`scopes`) — it scans nothing, so a directory that was never added stays invisible. The dashboard fields (`kind`/`study`/`priority`) are hand-edited or set by another tool and `sync` never touches them for a project it already knows. `path` is deliberately NOT required: a machine-specific absolute path has no business in a shipped seed (`assets/projects.default.json` pre-seeds dashboard metadata for well-known names before anyone has ever added them on a given machine), and `,proj.sh open` on an entry with no `path` yet fails with its own clear message pointing at `add` rather than the schema pretending every entry is immediately usable.

projects.description: Key is the project name, exactly as `,proj.sh list` prints it.

path.description: Absolute path to the project's directory, written by `,proj.sh add` (and re-pointed by `sync`). Absent on an entry nothing has added yet (e.g. a shipped seed name not present on this machine) — `,proj.sh open` refuses with its own message rather than opening a project with nowhere to open.

windows.description: The kitty window template, in open order — the project's tabs: one project window per entry, each launched with role tag `slot:<entry>` (`,proj.sh`'s `stamp_slot`). `nvim` gets a control socket for the graceful-quit path and `yazi` runs as the tab it opens (quitting yazi ends the window — see `,proj.sh`'s header comment); every other entry opens a plain shell. Source: `.proj.toml`'s `windows =` (repo root), defaulting to `["nvim", "yazi", "zsh", "run"]`.

workspace.description: Hyprland workspace `default_name` this project's windows open onto (only the initial placement; a window moves freely afterward). Source: `.proj.toml`/tms `workspace =`, defaulting to `code`.

scopes.description: A project's own working contexts beyond the fixed `windows` template — "like scenes but for projects": name to shell command, each spawned with role tag `slot:<name>` (the same tag vocabulary `windows` entries carry) and joined into the project's group by class. Source: `.proj.toml`'s `[scopes]` table (repo root), one plain `name = "command"` per line; absent or `{}` means the project declares none. `,proj.sh scope <name>` / `pick-scope` resolve against whichever project's group is focused, never a hardcoded name.

kind.description: What the dashboard shows this project as.

study.description: At most one project should carry this. The morning-restore routine (hypr start.lua) opens this project on workspace 1.
